note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 against HEAD 5c2cb2199f (independent judge, after ebae55f243, ea3bab5f48, a965d7c0d4). Section 2.9: "If the responder's policy allows it to accept the first selector of TSi and TSr, then the responder MUST narrow the Traffic Selectors to a subset that includes the initiator's first choices." narrowSelectors is unchanged: the (proposedI[0], proposedR[0]) intersections lead the answer. closedSubset changed in its doc only; its body keeps the first pair whenever crossPairs of that pair's own selectors yields the pair, which now requires matching protocols and families, and acceptablePairs (ea3bab5f48) refuses any combination that fails either, so the first acceptable pair is always kept. The new empty-subset guard in narrowChildSelectors fires only on a first pair acceptablePairs already refuses. a965d7c0d4: substituteVirtualIP rewrites proposed TSi to the lease for pool-bound peers. That can drop or reorder entries (a TSi of a family with no lease), but the bullet's condition, a policy that accepts the first selector, holds for a pool-bound peer only when TSi[0] is the lease host, and then the substituted TSi[0] is the same lease /32 with its port and protocol kept, so the first choice still leads. The substitution's separate defect (an answer outside the proposal) is RFC7296-2.9-1's, judged weak there. Tagged carriers TestNarrowingIncludesFirstChoice (both polarities: first choice leads when accepted, second choice leads when the first is refused), TestAuthResponsePayloadsCarryTheNarrowedSelectors, TestRFC7296TransportResponderNarrowsToFirstPair and TestPeerInitiatedRekeyIsNarrowedInTheExchangeOrientation PASS at HEAD. ./le rfc discriminate id RFC7296-2.9-2: one record (oneTransportPair pairs[:1] -> pairs), none stale; four claims unproven, judged by reading: TestNarrowingIncludesFirstChoice goes red if (0,0) is skipped or another pair leads (got[0] checked on both halves). Observation, verdict-neutral: the firstChoice/rest split in narrowSelectors is behaviourally identical to one pass in proposal order, because i==0,r==0 is the first iteration, so no mutant of the split can be observed. Verdict stands.
